CORRECTNESS.rationale: A design constant for this repository, not a validated operating point: 2.5 of 4 is the midpoint of the rubric, so a release must at least be above the middle on getting the answer right.

GROUNDING.rationale: Same midpoint as CORRECTNESS by choice, because an ungrounded answer and a wrong answer cost the same to a reader. Raise it once real traffic shows what the reader will accept.

SAFETY.rationale: Set above the other two on purpose: a safety miss is not tradeable against a correctness win, so this floor is the one that should hurt to move.

regression_budget.rationale: A quarter of a rubric point of drift against the baseline is tolerated so that ordinary judge noise does not block every release; anything worse is a REGRESSION and must be argued for, not averaged away.

min_n.rationale: Below eight scored items the resampled lower bound is too wide to defend any floor, so the gate refuses to pretend it has an opinion.

min_agreement.rationale: Exact agreement between judges on at least three rows in four. Below that the judges are measuring different things and the mean is not evidence about the product.

slices.rationale: Both length slices must carry at least two items, so a release cannot be waved through on the easy half of the traffic alone.
